body: I have looked into it and the issue is generic for FileDialogs in Godot. I have looked into fixing it, but it looks like it hits a design problem once multiple files are in play. So I looked into how other native file dialogs handle it. If it fits as a proposal better, let me know. GTK open file dialog always has some file selected and has no line edit box. Only filter textbox opens up if you type anything. Open button is always open but it makes sense in their case. KDialog open file(s) dialog selects from zero to many elements. Line edit box is always in sync with selection - all valid elements are selected. However, one thing how KDialog is different from Godot file dialog is that KDialog has multiple filenames in text box when multiple files are needed. Another thing is how deselecting works in KDialog. If input line edit box doesn't contain valid element, clicking empty space does nothing. But if there's at least one valid file selected, it will deselect all. KDialog always has open button enabled, but if input is empty, it literally does nothing - no error, no message. In Godot case, synchronizing Open button is not a problem, I have fixed it in my local branch, it's just not updated enough times. However, Godot has only one file in input line edit box at maximum, which causes a design problem of keeping it synchronized when multiple items are selected. Ideally, for me it makes sense that selected items would be the source of truth, are the ones which are passed as result, and everything is synchronized around them. Currently, it is like that, which is nice, though the input box is kinda problematic from design point of view. Either KDialog approach of multiple files makes sense, which is verbose, or GTK way of input box just being a filter could work.

> GTK open file dialog always has some file selected and has no line edit box. Only filter textbox opens up if you type anything.

That's interesting 🤔
Godot's FileDialog does have a filter box, which is separate from the filename box. I guess in Open mode the filename does not make much sense.

Alternatively, we could do both treat the selection as the only source of truth. If you type anything in the filename field, the dialog would try to select it in the list. If nothing is selected, Open is disabled. When selecting multiple files, the filename could show any of the selected files (e.g. the last one), and it would be impossible to select multiple files using the filename field.
